subject: VPC integration audit: control-plane / data-plane blueprint and failover scenarios
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-edge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@colossus-cloud.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: Private VPC integration - control/data blueprint for audit

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for taking this on. Attached is our current VPC blueprint and an egress matrix — we want Redwood's confirmation that the proposed control-plane attachment and data-plane routing meet our compliance constraints (no customer data egress without TLS + KMS, segmented admin lanes, and emergency failover to the colo).

Specific asks:
- Quick read of the control-plane ingress/egress boundaries and whether the plan isolates KV caches and runtime telemetry from tenant data paths.
- Validation of the proposed failover: if primary control-plane region BGP flaps, will traffic flow to the colo transit without exposing management APIs?
- Any ops/runbook gaps you see for the post-cutover ramp (first 48h).

Attachments: vpc_blueprint_v2.pdf (diagram), egress_matrix.xlsx (policy), controlplane-failover-snippets.txt (example commands).

If possible we'd like a short sync with your network lead this week — Wed/Thu morning PT works for us.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Senior EdgeOps Manager, Acme Financial
[Attachment: vpc_blueprint_v2.pdf (diagram)]
[Attachment: egress_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-edge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@colossus-cloud.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Private VPC integration - control/data blueprint for audit

Priya — thanks for the docs. Quick read-through notes below; I'm pulling Marissa (network lead), Irene (ops), and Naomi (compliance) into the thread for nitty-gritty items.

Top-level observations:
- Control-plane demarc looks correct conceptually: separate control-plane SUBNETS behind a management NACL, control-plane NAT via a dedicated NAT gateway. Need to confirm that management plane egress is restricted to Redwood-managed KMS endpoints (no wide internet).
- Data-plane attachment uses a BGP session into their transit; the diagram implies a shared AS for vendor transit. We'll require BGP MD5 and prefix filters on both sides and explicit route-ownership tagging to prevent accidental leak.
- KV cache isolation: diagram shows a shared internal subnet for the cache. We prefer caches in a dedicated tenancy/SG with strict ACLs per-tenant or per-slice (we can enumerate options below).

Questions / missing detail we need from you before we run the audit checklist:
1) Can you confirm whether the colo failover path uses a private L3 link (MPLS/Direct Connect) or public internet VPN? The failover semantics differ.
2) What KMS provider is in-scope for this deployment (Acme KMS vs. Redwood KMS via peered VPC)?
3) Any regulatory doc requirement for retaining audit logs in-region for 365 days (affects where telemetry is forwarded).

Marissa — can you review the proposed BGP/prefix plan and call out mandatory filters/rate-limits?
Irene — please look at the 48h ramp runbook gaps; I've attached the controlplane snippet but we need your ops playbook additions.
Naomi — any immediate compliance red flags from what Priya sent?

We can do a 30m sync Wed 9:30am PT; if that works I'll send a calendar invite with the checklist.

--
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: controlplane-failover-snippets.txt]

From: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-edge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@colossus-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Private VPC integration - control/data blueprint for audit

Thanks Jonas — answers inline below.

On Mon, Jun 4, 2028 at 11:03 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm whether the colo failover path uses a private L3 link (MPLS/Direct Connect) or public internet VPN?

We use a private L3 LAG into the colo (Direct Connect equivalent) — failover uses a secondary transit provider over private links, not public VPN.

> 2) What KMS provider is in-scope for this deployment (Acme KMS vs. Redwood KMS via peered VPC)?

Primary is Acme KMS (HSM-backed). We can supply RBAC lists and token scoping. Redwood KMS peering is not allowed for this environment.

> 3) Any regulatory doc requirement for retaining audit logs in-region for 365 days

Yes — EU and UK subsidiaries require 365d in-region retention for customer traffic logs (we'll annotate which tenants fall under that).

Extra notes:
- Cache: we currently have a shared cache for performance; replacing with tenant-scoped caches adds ~8-12% latency in our bench but meets compliance. If Redwood can offer explicit per-tenant cache ACLs at the network layer that might be an acceptable middle ground.
- BGP: we'll enable MD5; Carlos will share the prefix plan tonight.
- Runbook: we can provide the first-24h monitoring checklist; we want Redwood to own the control-plane health dashboard and rapid rollback hooks.

Wed 9:30am PT works. I'll bring Carlos and our network architect.

Regards,
Priya Sharma
Senior EdgeOps Manager, Acme Financial

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial: Private VPC integration - control/data blueprint and next steps

Priya / team — brief summary and proposed action items from our side before the sync: 

Summary of acceptance constraints we will validate in the audit:
- Control-plane must only egress to Acme KMS endpoints (no public KMS peering).
- KV caches must not be able to route tenant plaintext traffic; implement either per-tenant cache subnets or network-level ACLs mapped to tenant tags.
- BGP sessions: MD5 + prefix-lists + max-prefix + route-owner tags. No default-route injection from the transit.
- Telemetry: we will implement an in-region aggregator for EU/UK tenants and forward 365d retention to Acme's logging bucket; redact sensitive PII fields before forwarding.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) Jonas: produce a short technical checklist (15 items) for Wed sync — includes ACL examples, test cases for failover, and quick remediation commands. (ETA: Wed 08:00 PT)
2) Irene: draft 48h runbook addendum for control-plane cutover + rollback steps. (ETA: Fri 12:00 PT)
3) Naomi: confirm compliance mapping for EU/UK tenants and required telemetry fields redaction. (ETA: Thu EOD)
4) Priya / Carlos: share the final prefix plan and colo L3 circuit IDs before the meeting.

Meeting confirm: Wed 9:30am PT — invite sent. Please attach any lane diagrams or ACL snippets to the calendar item.

We're aligned on the big constraints; the audit will focus on proving isolation and safe failover without management-plane exposure. Look forward to the meeting.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: checklist-template.md referenced in invite]
